Explain in your own words what 'Rotation of the Earth' refers to.
questions.a: The spinning movement of the Earth around its own imaginary axis, which takes approximately 24 hours to complete.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Rotation of the Earth'.
questions.a: Rotation causes the daily cycle of day and night.

How many days are in a regular year? Use the method 'Revolution and Leap Year'. Work with: the fixed constants of the method. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of total_days.
Explain in your own words what 'Revolution and Leap Year' refers to.
questions.a: The Earth's orbital movement around the Sun, taking 365.25 days, where the extra quarter-days accumulate to form a leap year every four years.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Revolution and Leap Year'.
questions.a: Revolution causes seasonal changes and the leap year cycle.

Take the relation taught for 'Solstice and Equinox' and work with: night_length = 30. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of equinox_day_length.
Explain in your own words what 'Solstice and Equinox' refers to.
questions.a: Solstices are points in the orbit where one hemisphere receives maximum sunlight, while equinoxes are points where the Sun shines directly on the equator.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Solstice and Equinox'.
questions.a: Tilt of the Earth's axis relative to the orbital plane determines seasonal intensity.
